previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of bronchopulmonary dysplasia, tracheobronchomalacia, and tracheostomy dependence was admitted for increased yellow, blood-tinged tracheostomy secretions, neck pain, and shortness of breath. She was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics for suspected tracheobronchitis. A CT scan showed chronic subglottic stenosis but no acute infection. She underwent a flexible bronchoscopy with excision of granulation tissue, which improved her symptoms. Antibiotics were narrowed to ciprofloxacin based on clinical findings and gram stain showing gram-positive cocci. Her respiratory status improved, and she was discharged home on a 7-day course of oral ciprofloxacin with follow-up arranged with ENT and interventional pulmonology. Chronic conditions including asthma, GERD, depression, anxiety, and chronic pain were managed with continued home medications.

by speech and swallow for speaking valve, but she was unable to
